q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of refractory bricks per tonne?
title: Refractory brick carbon per tonne
short: Add the kiln fuel at its IPCC default factor and plant electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, divide by tonnes fired, then add raw materials such as fireclay, alumina or magnesia from supplier data. Raw materials that release CO2 when fired, such as magnesite, add process CO2.
audience: Refractory makers and steel, cement and glass plants that buy refractories

ul: Kiln firing at high temperature: Scope 1 fuel.
Crushing, mixing and pressing power: Scope 2.
Bought-in calcined raw materials, with their own footprint.
Process CO2 if carbonates are fired on site.

p: If you calcine magnesite or dolomite yourself, count the CO2 released from the carbonate by chemistry, from the mass fired, as Scope 1 process emissions.
Steel and cement plants may ask for refractory footprints in supplier surveys. Give the plant figure per tonne and the raw material factors with their sources.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per tonne (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Add raw materials (fireclay, alumina, magnesia) from supplier data
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; firing fuel varies a lot by product and kiln type.
